source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:1 ('וישמע — REVIA on the mem')
claim_en: THE HEARING UNDER REVIA: וישמע ('and he HEARD the words of Laban's sons,' 31:1 — the unit's opening verb) carries revia (the pausing four-dot accent) on the mem exactly as ruled.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:1 ('את כל הכבד — NO maqqef between את and the all-word')
claim_en: THE OBJECT-WORD UNJOINED: את of 'he has made ALL THIS WEALTH' (31:1) stands free — no maqqef (the joining stroke) binding it to the all-word, exactly as Minchat Shai rules, its tzere and merkha carried on its own.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:1 ('הכבד — lean, no vav; and every other glory-word in the Torah whose kaf is in qamatz is written FULL')
claim_en: THE GLORY WRITTEN LIKE THE LIVER: הכבד ('all this WEALTH,' 31:1 — the riches Laban's sons begrudge) is the glory-word written LEAN, no vav, against the fullness of every other qamatz-kaf glory in the Torah — and the lean skeleton is exactly the skeleton of הכבד THE LIVER: the other eleven tokens of these letters in the Torah are all the liver-lobe of the altar (Exodus and Leviticus, bet in tzere, builder-checked one by one). The begrudged wealth written one vav short, into the letters of the organ burned whole on the fire.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:2 ('כתמול שלשום — BOTH full; so in all the precise books and the Hilleli copy; the printer who wrote the first lean erred')
claim_en: YESTERDAY WRITTEN WHOLE AT THE SEEING: כתמול שלשום ('and Jacob SAW Laban's face, and it was not toward him AS YESTERDAY AND THE DAY BEFORE,' 31:2) — both time-words carry their vav, full as the Hilleli and all the precise books rule, the printer's lean first word refuted in the stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:5 ('כתמל שלשם — BOTH lean; so in all the precise books; the Ramah lists this כתמל among the Torah's four lean yesterday-forms')
claim_en: AND WRITTEN BARE AT THE TELLING: three verses later Jacob repeats the same phrase to his wives — 'your father's face is not toward me AS YESTERDAY AND THE DAY BEFORE' (31:5) — and BOTH words drop their vav: the identical idiom, seen full in the narrator's mouth and lean in Jacob's, exactly as the precise books and the Ramah's lean-list rule. What Jacob SAW was whole; what he could SAY of it had already thinned.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:2 ('the Ramah: every yesterday-form in the Torah is FULL except FOUR lean — Gen 31:5, Exod 21:29, Deut 4:42, Deut 19:4; and the Hilleli Masorah: שלשום full exactly TWICE in the Torah — Gen 31:2 and Deut 19:6')
claim_en: THE ONE VERSE THAT CROSSES BOTH COUNTS: on SNAPSHOT the from-yesterday form מתמול stands full four times (Exod 4:10, Exod 21:36, Deut 4:42, Deut 19:6) — but the Ramah rules Deut 4:42's token LEAN (his fourth lean member), and the Hilleli's two-full count of שלשום likewise excludes Deut 4:42, where SNAPSHOT again writes full. One verse — the cities-of-refuge debut — carries BOTH its yesterday-words plene against both camps' rulings: a two-word counted-law variance concentrated on a single verse, filed with the eleven-vs-eighteen class.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:3 ('שוב אל ארץ אבותיך — this one ALONE in the Torah is written full vav and full yod; every other is אבתיך, lean vav')
claim_en: THE ONE FULL FATHERS: אבותיך ('RETURN to the land of YOUR FATHERS, and I will be with you,' 31:3 — the command that turns the whole unit) is the Torah's ONE fathers-of-yours written full with both vav and yod; the other fifteen tokens all run vav-lean (builder-counted). The word is written whole exactly once — at the command to go back to it.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 31:6 ('ואתנה — 3 in the Masorah: AND-YOU know (here), AND-YOU my flock, the flock of my pasture (Ezek 34:31), AND-YOU, hailstones (Ezek 13:11); as the flock of the pasture speaks of Israel, so the flock here is read on the exiles')
claim_en: THE PRONOUN AMONG THE GIVE-VERBS: ואתנה ('AND YOU know that with all my strength I served your father,' 31:6 — Jacob to Rachel and Leah) — the Torah writes these letters nine times, but eight are the verb 'and I will give'; only here do they stand as the feminine pronoun AND-YOU (the tagged form itself distinguishes them, builder-checked), and it is this pronoun the Masorah's three-list counts, its two companions both in Ezekiel, named — the flock of the pasture that is Israel, and the hailstones.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:7 ('התל בי — the he in TZERE in all the books, and the letter rests in place of the dagesh that ought to stand in the tav; the printer multiplied words and his own deceived heart misled him')
claim_en: THE MOCKING-VERB'S LONG E: התל ('your father has MOCKED me and changed my wage ten counts,' 31:7) — the he in tzere (the long e) with all the books, and the tav SOFT, the doubling dot it ought to carry resting unwritten, exactly as Minchat Shai rules — dismissing the printer with the verse's own verb: 'a deceived heart misled him.'

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:7 ('והחלף — the het with HATAF SEGOL, and lean without yod; so the Ramah: written lean of yod')
claim_en: THE CHANGE-VERB LEAN: והחלף ('and he CHANGED my wage ten counts,' 31:7) — the het in hataf segol (the compound half-vowel) and the word lean, its i-vowel carried by the point with no yod, exactly as Minchat Shai and the Ramah rule: the wage-changing written one letter short.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:14 ('ותאמרנה — the Masorah marks it: NONE like it full in the Torah — full with he; the rest of the Torah written without the he, ending in bare nun; and the precise copies all agree')
claim_en: THE ONE FULL AND-THEY-SAID: ותאמרנה ('and Rachel and Leah answered AND SAID to him,' 31:14) — the Torah's ONE feminine group-speech written full with its closing he; its two bare sisters ותאמרן are the midwives before Pharaoh (Exod 1:19) and the well-daughters of Midian (Exod 2:19), builder-checked: three companies of women speak in the Torah, and only the wives consenting to the return speak with the word written whole.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:10 ('ואשא עיני — the shin with maarich [the Sephardic name of the merkha stroke], and the nun with TEVIR, not zaqef qatan')
claim_en: THE DREAM-LIFT'S RULED MUSIC: ואשא עיני ('and I LIFTED MY EYES and saw in a dream,' 31:10) — the merkha (the Sephardic maarich) on the lift-verb's shin and TEVIR on the eyes-word's nun, against the zaqef qatan camp, both exactly as Minchat Shai rules: the accent-pair of the dream's opening carried mark for mark.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:17 ('הגמלים — the gimel DAGESHED')
claim_en: THE CAMELS' DOUBLING DOT: הגמלים ('he set his sons and his wives on THE CAMELS,' 31:17 — the flight mounted) — the gimel dageshed exactly as ruled.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:18 ('רכשו — an old scroll-manual records רכושו full per most books; but I have already written at Gen 14 in the Ramah's name that it is LEAN, and so we hold')
claim_en: HIS PROPERTY WRITTEN LEAN: רכשו ('and he led away... all HIS PROPERTY that he had gathered,' 31:18) — lean, the u-vowel carried by the point alone, with Minchat Shai and the Ramah against the old scroll-manual's most-books full form: the flight's inventory-word one vav short, as at Abram's wars (Gen 14).

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:5; Onkelos Genesis 31:19
claim_en: ONE EMBARRASSMENT, TWO TRACKS, AND THIS IS THE CLEANEST INSTANCE IN THE SWEEP. The theft of the images is defended in the chain by intent - shall I go my way and leave this elder in his corruption? - and the chain insists that the verse must therefore still SAY 'stole', the act named and the motive supplied. Onkelos takes the other route entirely and changes the verb: she HID the images; he CONCEALED his intentions rather than stole the heart; he WENT rather than fled. The midrash keeps the word and argues the intent; the translation keeps the intent and removes the word. Two members of one declared shelf solving one embarrassment by opposite means at the same verses.

check.note: One difficulty solved by supplying motive in the midrash and by demoting the verb in the translation, at the same verses.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:4
claim_en: A CURSE UTTERED IN IGNORANCE IS TRACKED AS AN OPERATIVE CAUSE ACROSS FOUR CHAPTERS. R. Yosei builds the chain explicitly: she stole at 31:19, the curse was pronounced at 31:32 - with whomever you find your gods, he shall not live - and she died at 35:19, the whole compared to an error that issues from a ruler. It stands beside R. Yudan's rival cause, that she spoke before her elder sister, and beside the burial-price account already recorded at gen_51. Three separate explanations of one death, all kept, one of them a mechanism the machine can follow verse by verse.

check.note: A curse tracked as an operative cause across three verses in different blocks, with two rival explanations preserved.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:1
claim_en: THE RETURN COMMAND CARRIES A DOCTRINE ABOUT WHERE PROPERTY CAN BE BLESSED. Reish Lakish states it as a rule: possessions outside the land carry no blessing - so the promise attached to the command is conditioned on the return itself. The chain records the objection from a wealthy neighbouring territory and the contrast case of a leader blessed wherever he goes, against a householder who is told to go home. And the land is defined by a property of its dead rather than of its living.

check.note: A blessing on property made conditional on geography, with its counterexample and a leader-versus-householder distinction recorded.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 73:12
claim_en: THE FLIGHT'S TRIGGER IS TRACED THROUGH THREE STAGES AND ONE OF THEM IS A FACE. The sons' words come first, and the chain notes why sons exist to speak them - the household had daughters herding flocks until this man's arrival - then the countenance changes, with a named sage quoted on a man's heart changing his face for good or ill, and only then the command: your father-in-law scowls at you and you sit here? Return, and I will be with you. A causal chain assembled from a rumour, an expression, and an instruction.

check.note: A three-stage causal trigger assembled from reported speech, a facial change, and a command.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:2
claim_en: A PRUDENCE RULE IS DERIVED FROM WHERE THE CONVERSATION WAS HELD. That the counsel was taken in the open field yields the rule about speaking secrets, put as a proverb - in a field with mounds, speak no secrets - alongside three praises of the region's people. The verse's setting, not its content, is what carries the law.

check.note: A prudence rule derived from a scene's location rather than its speech.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:5
claim_en: A LEXICAL RULE IS STATED AND CARRIED ACROSS THREE FIGURES. Wherever shearing is mentioned, the chain holds, it MAKES AN IMPRESSION - a portent verb - and names three figures at whose shearing something turned. The rule is re-witnessed at a second seat elsewhere in the corpus. The same section separately reads the order of loading, sons before wives, against the brother's inverse order at his own departure.

check.note: A verb declared portentous wherever it occurs, with three named instances and a second witnessing seat.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:9
claim_en: THE SEARCH SCENE IS GIVEN THREE LAYERS, ENDING IN A MERCY. The searcher enters her tent twice because he knew she was a TOUCHER, one who handles everything - a motif the chain has carried since the account of the woman's creation. The concealment under the saddle-cushion follows. And then the mercy: R. Yochanan holds the images BECAME JUGS so that she would not be shamed. Suspicion, concealment, and transformation, in that order, at one scene.

check.note: A search scene layered as suspicion, concealment, and a transformation performed to prevent shame.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 82:3
claim_en: THE MEDIUM OF BOTH APPEARANCES IS MADE UNIFORM BY A LATER VERSE. Reading that God appeared AGAIN as at first, the chain concludes that both appearances were BY AN ANGEL, matching this block's own dream verse in which the angel of God speaks. A claim about the mechanism of revelation established by comparing two verses' descriptions rather than by assertion.

check.note: The medium of a revelation fixed by comparing an 'again, as at first' verse with this block's dream description.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 92:8
claim_en: THE THEFT ECHOES INTO THE NEXT GENERATION AS A TAUNT. When a cup is found in the youngest brother's sack, the taunt is thief, son of a thief - reaching back to this block's theft - and his retort is recorded with it: is the man who sold Joseph here? A narrative act entered into the record with a downstream consequence in another block, and the retort preserved rather than the accusation alone.

check.note: An act generating a taunt in a later block, with the accused's counter-accusation preserved alongside.

source: Onkelos Genesis 31:19; Onkelos Genesis 31:30
claim_en: THE OPPONENT'S GODS ARE NEVER CALLED GODS IN THE TRANSLATION. The household images are rendered as IMAGES, and where their owner says 'my gods' the translation gives MY OBJECT OF FEAR. A contempt policy applied consistently: the buffer will not let the word for deity stand in that mouth, and it repeats the choice at the echo verse.

check.note: A consistent refusal to render an opponent's deity-word as deity, applied at every occurrence in the block.
